title: Émile Zola's birth chart
metaDescription: Émile Zola's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.8° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Aries — the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Mars and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 12.8° Aries: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Sun. A fire sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 21.7° Aries, Venus at 13.2° Pisces, Mars at 20.3° Aries. Mercury in a fire sign reads as a mind that decides at speaking speed; Venus in a water sign reads as taste tuned to mood and undertow; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mercury trine Saturn, 0.0° of separation. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, Jupiter trine Uranus at 0.3°, and Mercury conjunction Mars at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 12.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 13.2° is in exaltation; Mars in Aries at 20.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements fire 6, water 3, air 1; modalities cardinal 5, mutable 3, fixed 2. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.5° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 10.8°.
